long_biography.plain_text:
Arlec was a core asset in Ian Trahar’s business platform while Avatar Industries owned the electrical-products supplier in the late 1990s. A Trahar-controlled entity bought the business from listed Avatar in 2007. He remains an Arlec director and the controlling shareholder of its UK holding company. Arlec’s brands, inventories and operations belong to its corporate entities; Trahar’s connection is through ownership and governance.

Trahar’s wider interests sit in separate companies rather than one operating group. He is non-executive chairman of listed aquaculture company Seafarms Group and controls Avatar Finance, a lender and shareholder associated with that company. He is also executive chairman of environmental-services provider CO2 Australia, which was demerged from Seafarms. He holds an MBA from the University of Melbourne and is a member of the Australian Institute of Company Directors.

uncertainties.detail: Arlec is the strongest documented private operating interest and the directly reported source of Trahar's fortune. Public records also show material interests in finance, environmental services and aquaculture, but they do not provide comparable current private valuations. Fashion & Retail is therefore used for both creation and primary industry without treating every controlled or associated company as a personal asset.

Sources establish a banking and investment career, the Trahar-controlled purchase of Arlec and the absence of any evidenced inheritance of the core business. They do not establish whether a substantial family or social advantage shaped his start, so the broad Self-made classification is used rather than either starting-position subtype.

Trahar is currently an Arlec director, Seafarms non-executive chairman and controller of Avatar Finance; Business News also lists him as CO2 Australia's executive chairman. His joint chief executive role at Avatar Industries and executive positions at Shell Australia and Citibank are historical and are described accordingly.

Companies House documents Trahar's personal control of Arlec UK Holdings, while Australian filings identify corporate entities controlled by or associated with him. The dossier treats those entities' brands, inventories, operating assets, loans and public-company shares as company property or equity interests, not as directly owned personal assets.

No strong public source established a secondary nationality, place or country of birth, exact birth day, suffix or secondary residence. Existing Australian nationality, residence, July 1955 birth details and alive status were corroborated rather than reproposed.

No identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website cleared the confidence threshold. Arlec's official domain is proposed only as Company Website. Volatile wealth estimates, changing transactions, disputes, private matters and all vessel context were excluded.
